questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the sentences in the correct

logical sequence to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

a. It regulates the operation of all body organs and protects the body and mind from becoming unbalanced as a result of

negative circumstances and unhealthy lifestyles.

b. It only requires frequent practice of the proper body motions and breathing techniques.

c. The physical benefits of yoga can be enjoyed for a lifetime without risk or injury.

d. It regulates the relationship between the body, the intellect, and the spirit.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option (2)** i.e. **c, b, d, a**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence starts with "The physical benefits of yoga can be enjoyed for a lifetime without risk or injury," which is correctly indicated by **part (c).**
 
• Following the introduction, "It only requires frequent practice of the proper body motions and breathing techniques" **(b)** continues the logical sequence, explaining the requirement for achieving those benefits.
 
• **The next part,** "It regulates the relationship between the body, the intellect, and the spirit," elaborates on the benefits mentioned, indicated by **(d).**
 
• **Ending with,** "It regulates the operation of all body organs and protects the body and mind from becoming unbalanced as a result of negative circumstances and unhealthy lifestyles" **(a)** completes the explanation by describing the holistic impact of yoga.

Therefore, the correct answer is **c, b, d, a.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (d, a, b, c):** This option disrupts the logical flow, starting with a general statement about regulation and ending with the benefits of yoga, which is less coherent.
 
• **Option 3 (b, a, c, d):** This option places the requirement of practice before mentioning the benefits, making the initial statement unclear.
 
• **Option 4 (a, b, c, d):** This option starts with a detailed function of yoga instead of introducing the benefits first, which is less effective for understanding the overall advantages.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Nina has not yet learned how to __straighten up and fly right__.

options.text: forget the wrongdoings of the others
improve her absurd behaviour and act seriously
be professional in flying the aircraft
remember the past and prepare for the future

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The phrase "**straighten up and fly right**" is an idiomatic expression meaning to improve one's behavior, act properly, and conduct oneself correctly.
 
• It does not refer to piloting an aircraft or addressing the past, rather it focuses on correcting one's improper behavior and becoming more responsible.
 
• Thus, the most appropriate substitution is **improve her absurd behaviour and act seriously**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Nina has not yet learned how to improve her absurd behaviour and act seriously."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Option 1: "forget the wrongdoings of the others"** – This does not capture the meaning of improving one's own behavior.
 
• **Option 3: "be professional in flying the aircraft"** – This is a literal interpretation involving aviation, which is unrelated to the idiomatic context of the sentence.
 
• **Option 4: "remember the past and prepare for the future"** – This is about reflecting on the past and planning ahead, which, although good advice, does not convey the essence of improving inappropriate behavior.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

I had __not only helped her by__ giving hints but also with providing her links.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The phrase "not only... but also" is used to connect two related actions, emphasizing that both actions were done.
 
• The correct format for this phrase in the sentence is: "helped her not only by giving hints but also by providing her links."
 
• Thus, the most appropriate substitution is **helped her not only by**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I had helped her not only by giving hints but also by providing her links."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Option 2: "helped her not by"** – This changes the intended meaning of the sentence and does not use the "not only... but also" structure correctly.
 
• **Option 3: "helped her only by"** – This implies that helping was limited to one action and does not reflect the intended emphasis of doing more than one thing.
 
• **Option 4: "helped not only her by"** – This is incorrect because it disrupts the proper structure and meaning of the phrase "not only... but also."

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Positive self-talk __have a great affect__ on one’s self-worth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The verb "have" should be "has" to agree with the singular subject "Positive self-talk."
 
• The correct noun is "effect" rather than "affect." "Effect" is the noun form that means a change that results from an action, whereas "affect" is usually a verb.
 
• Thus, the correct substitution is **has a great effect**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Positive self-talk has a great effect on one’s self-worth."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Option 1: "has a great affect"** – The word "affect" is incorrect here; "effect" is needed.
 
• **Option 2: "have a great effect"** – The verb "have" does not agree with the singular subject "Positive self-talk."
 
• **Option 3: "having a great affect"** – The structure "having" and the word "affect" are both incorrect in this context.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

He was given a reward for his contribution by the Governor.

options.text: For his contribution, he was rewarded by the governor.
The governor gave him a reward for his contribution.
Rewarded by the governor, as he contributed along.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "The governor gave him a reward for his contribution."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "a reward" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "gave" to "was given" (past simple passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "the governor."
 
• Ensure the phrase "for his contribution" remains for clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The governor gave him a reward for his contribution."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"For his contribution, he was rewarded by the governor." – This is a passive voice sentence.
 
• **Option 2: **"The governor rewarded him." – This is a correct active voice sentence but less detailed.
 
• **Option 4: **"Rewarded by the governor, as he contributed along." – This is an incomplete and incorrect sentence structure.

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "We have to say little in this matter."

• Change the active verb form "have to say" to "has to be said" (passive form).
